claude.sample_unit: radiologists (each reading 90 chest radiographs across 4 conditions)
models_evaluated: sham AI (simulated chest radiograph AI, ROC-AUC 0.87)

links.outcome: Radiologist false negative and false positive rates when AI results were incorrect versus no AI
links.effect: FN rose from 2.7% (No AI) to 33.0% (Keep, No Box), 26.7% (Delete), 20.7% (Box); FP rose from 51.4% to 86.0%, 80.5%, 80.5%.
links.quote: In total, incorrect AI results can cause radiologists to make incorrect decisions when they would have otherwise been correct.

links.outcome: Effect of AI box outlining suspicious region on radiologist errors from incorrect AI
links.effect: FNs lower with box than without (20.7% vs 33.0%, p=0.04); FPs 80.5% vs 86.0%, not significant (p=0.19).
links.quote: As anticipated in hypothesis 5, FNs were higher in AI Keep (No Box) than in AI Keep (Box) (33.0% vs. 20.7%, p = 0.04).

links.outcome: Reader performance with versus without AI, assessing overreliance on incorrect AI
links.effect: Compared with No AI, incorrect AI increased FN (2.7% to 20.7-33.0%) and FP (51.4% to 80.5-86.0%); correct AI improved accuracy.
links.quote: As anticipated, when AI provided correct positive and correct negative results, radiologists were more accurate in all AI conditions compared to the no AI condition.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in workflow, including interface configuration effects
links.effect: Human-AI performance depended on AI presentation: box reduced FNs (33.0% to 20.7%); keep vs delete affected FPs (86.0% vs 80.5%, p=0.03).
links.quote: There was evidence that the way AI was implemented impacted radiologist performance.

links.outcome: Radiologist susceptibility to incorrect AI (automation bias) with no training
links.effect: Incorrect AI increased false negatives to 20.7-33.0% and false positives to 80.5-86.0% among radiologists.
links.quote: But when AI provided false feedback that there was no abnormality, false negatives increased to 20.7–33.0%, depending on the AI results condition.

links.outcome: Missed cancers when AI labeled abnormal cases normal
links.effect: False negatives on the 4 AI-false-negative cases rose from 2.7% without AI to 33.0% (p=0.006) with kept AI results.
links.quote: Among these cases in the No AI condition, the false negative percent was 2.7% (95% CI (0.4, 16.0)); false negatives increased to 33.0% (95% CI (21.5, 46.9)) in the AI Keep (No Box) condition ( p = 0.006)

unlisted_practices: Telling radiologists AI results will be deleted from the patient record rather than kept, to reduce deference to incorrect AI

openai.sample_unit: chest radiographs from 90 patients read by 5 radiologists

links.effect: FNs rose from 2.7% to 20.7–33.0%; FPs from 51.4% to 80.5–86.0%.
links.quote: Relative to the No AI condition (FN = 2.7%, FP = 51.4%), FN and FPs were higher in the Keep AI (No Box) (FN = 33.0%, FP = 86.0%), Delete AI (No Box) (FN = 26.7%, FP = 80.5%), and Keep AI (Box) (FN = to 20.7%, FP = 80.5%) conditions (all ps < 0.05).

links.effect: FNs were 33.0% without box vs. 20.7% with box, p = 0.04.
links.quote: As anticipated in hypothesis 5, FNs were higher in AI Keep (No Box) than in AI Keep (Box) (33.0% vs. 20.7%, p = 0.04).

links.outcome: False negatives with visual AI output
links.effect: FNs were 33.0% without box vs. 20.7% with box, p = 0.04.
links.quote: As anticipated in hypothesis 5, FNs were higher in AI Keep (No Box) than in AI Keep (Box) (33.0% vs. 20.7%, p = 0.04).

unlisted_practices: Deleting AI results from the patient's file rather than keeping them

links.outcome: radiologist false negative rate when AI is incorrect
links.effect: False negatives increased from 2.7% without AI to 33.0% in Keep AI (No Box) (p=0.006), 26.7% in Delete AI (No Box) (p=0.009), and 20.7% in Keep AI (Box) (p=0.02).
links.quote: Among these cases in the No AI condition, the false negative percent was 2.7% (95% CI (0.4, 16.0)); false negatives increased to 33.0% (95% CI (21.5, 46.9)) in the AI Keep (No Box) condition ( p = 0.006), increased to 26.7% (95%CI (17.7, 38.1)) in the AI Delete (No Box) condition ( p = 0.009), and increased to 20.7% (95% CI (9.4, 39.6)) in the AI Keep (Box) condition ( p = 0.02).

links.outcome: radiologist false negative rate with visual bounding box
links.effect: False negatives were lower with a bounding box outlining suspicion than without a box (20.7% vs. 33.0%, p = 0.04).
links.quote: As anticipated in hypothesis 5, FNs were higher in AI Keep (No Box) than in AI Keep (Box) (33.0% vs. 20.7%, p = 0.04).

unlisted_practices: Not saving AI results to the patient record to reduce clinician liability concerns and conformity bias

screen.practice: AI UI design (bounding box display) and data retention policy framing
screen.reason: Evaluates how specific AI presentation/deployment factors (providing visual bounding boxes around lesions vs not, and whether AI findings are retained in the patient record) affect clinician decision-making and automation bias.
